technical_and_design_decisions: Treat the increment as work on a Spring Cloud Data Flow (formerly Spring XD) style platform, since the user stories reference admin/container servers, uber-jar modules, YARN, and Spark.
Use Spring Framework 6.0+ with Java 17+ as the baseline, as specified in the preamble.
U4 and U5 are identical (verbatim duplicates); they are merged into a single implementation activity to avoid double counting.
U2 is explicitly scoped as a Spike (research/design only, not full implementation). Only design specs, approach identification, DSL/UI scoping, and next-step documentation are in scope.
U3 is scoped as a performance investigation (profiling and analysis), not a code change activity. Output is bottleneck identification and pros/cons documentation.
RxJava processor (U1) is implemented as an adapter/processor module that conforms to the platform's existing processor SPI so it can be plugged into pipelines.
HDFS storage (U4/U5) is implemented as a pluggable module registry backend with HA-aware read/reinstall semantics, leveraging Hadoop FileSystem APIs.
Location overrides (U6/U7) are implemented as externalized configuration properties (e.g., Spring @ConfigurationProperties) rather than code changes, to allow environment-specific overrides.
Spark job stop (U8) is implemented using Spark's REST API (or the existing deployment SPI) to cancel the job and free cluster resources.
Each implementation activity includes unit tests; a dedicated integration test activity covers end-to-end scenarios.
assumptions: A single developer performs all activities; an 8-hour workday is the effort unit.
The codebase, build system (Gradle/Maven), CI, and local Spring XD/SCDF environment are already in place; only incremental additions are needed.
U4 and U5 are duplicates and treated as one feature.
U2 (ACL) deliverable is a design document only — no production code, no DSL/UI implementation.
U3 (performance) deliverable is a profiling report and recommendations — no refactoring code changes.
Profiling tools (e.g., JFR, async-profiler, YourKit) are available and authorized for use.
Hadoop/Spark clusters and HDFS are available in a dev/test environment for verification.
Requirements elicitation and stakeholder reviews beyond the spike are out of scope.
No production deployment, operations handover, or runbook authoring is included.
Code review and small rework loops are absorbed within each activity estimate.

activities.activity_description: Set up incremental module structure, update build files, add required dependencies (RxJava, HDFS/Hadoop client, Spark client, Spring Security ACL), and ensure baseline builds and tests pass.

Design and implement a flexible RxJava-based processor module conforming to the platform's processor SPI, supporting reactive stream composition and back-pressure. Includes unit tests for typical processor contracts.

Review customer use cases for per-user/resource ACLs, evaluate approaches against XD runtime, identify DSL and UI scope, and produce a design spec with next steps and proposed phases. No production code.
Profile admin server and container server startup, isolate CPU hotspots, document root causes, and provide a pros/cons analysis of potential remedies. No code refactor delivered.

Implement HDFS as a storage backend for custom module uber-jars, including HA-aware reads and reliable reinstall semantics under failure scenarios. Includes configuration wiring and unit/integration tests.
Expose HDFS location as an externalized configuration property so users can override where the custom module uber-jar is stored and retrieved. Includes property binding, validation, and tests.
Expose YARN config location as an externalized configuration property so users can override where the custom module uber-jar is stored and retrieved. Includes property binding, validation, and tests.

activities.activity_name: Stop Spark job and resource cleanup (U8)
activities.activity_description: Implement a mechanism to stop a running Spark job, perform graceful shutdown, and clean up associated cluster resources at completion. Includes unit and integration tests against a Spark deployment.

End-to-end integration tests covering HDFS HA scenarios, configuration overrides, Spark job stop lifecycle, and the RxJava processor within sample pipelines. Verify no regression in admin/container startup.
Update user/operator documentation: new properties for HDFS/YARN overrides, RxJava processor usage, Spark stop operation, and link to the ACL spike and profiling reports.
